legend: The range of appearances is broad; some examples arise in a pigmented patch; others, like this example, are amelanotic, level with the surface or elevated (as shown here), and (often) indurated.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma with so-called neural transforming areas in the lip of a 24-year-old woman
legend: Thick neuroid bundles are present in the upper dermis; there are also occasional atypical junctional melanocytes, a few subepidermal spindle cells, and scattered lymphocytes.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma with so-called neural transforming areas in the lip of a 24-year-old woman
legend: A neuroid bundle (top) contains atypical elongated spindle nuclei; intraneural and perineural involvement of a small nerve is also present. There is a prominent infiltrate of lymphocytes.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma with so-called neural transforming areas in the lip of a 24-year-old woman
legend: Atypical spindle cells, some with elongated nuclei, are admixed with lymphocytes.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma in the cheek of a 73-year-old man
legend: The increased cellularity in the dermis is due mainly to spindled melanocytes and lymphocytes; there is also patchy solar elastosis, deep acute haemorrhage, and epidermal thickening.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma in the cheek of a 73-year-old man
legend: A few atypical enlarged melanocytes are present in the junctional zone. The fibrohistiocytic pattern is accompanied by scattered lymphocytes, some in clusters; mitoses are rare.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma in the cheek of a 73-year-old man
legend: Atypical spindle cells with elongated nuclei appear to be within and between collagen bundles.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma in the forearm of a 76-year-old woman
legend: Abnormal junctional melanocytes and dermal spindle cells with patchy lymphocytes.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic melanoma in the scalp of a 68-year-old man
legend: This punch biopsy specimen was originally diagnosed as a scar; only an occasional spindle cell was S100-positive, and no abnormal junctional melanocytes were found. A larger desmoplastic melanoma was removed from the same site 6 months later; clues to the diagnosis are the small foci of lymphocytes and the haphazard permeation of the dermal zone of elastosis by spindle cells.
Scattered atypical spindle cells in dermis show nuclear expression of SOX10 with red chromogen.
